rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the latest first working day: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03 -> 01.04). It must always be the 1st of a month and follows every change of the first working day.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status is entered at the fund from its list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed). Provisionally, Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married.

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, married and registered partnership count as married; single, divorced, separated and widowed count as single, as in the calculator.

rules.name: Spouse exemption from source tax
rules.statement: An employee who is married or in a registered partnership with a spouse/partner who lives in Switzerland and is Swiss or holds a C permit is not subject to source tax. Separated employees count as single and get no exemption.
rules.expression: civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "yes")

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is always subject to source tax, whatever the nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss (Swiss citizenship counts even with another nationality), without a C permit, and not exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse/partner living in Switzerland. Only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions.
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and (civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"] or (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_residence_country != "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "no"))))

rules.name: Residence for the source tax tariff
rules.statement: The calculator's 'main residence in Switzerland' and 'state of residence' answers are derived from the home address country: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein, or other country. Switzerland and other countries leave the base tariff unchanged; Germany and Liechtenstein open the cross-border questions.

rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose child result is 'counts' or 'counts as H child' (0 if no children). Evaluated per child and summed over all children.

rules.name: Single-parent H tariff

rules.statement: Base letter: married -> C (spouse works) or B (spouse does not); single -> H if any child counts as H child, otherwise A. If the cross-border tariff applies, the letter is mapped A->L, B->M, C->N, H->P.

rules.name: Source tax result
rules.statement: Lonio computes the source tax result for every employee subject to source tax and records it for HR: the full tariff code = tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y). Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days get 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' flagged for HR; with more than 45 days the tariff code subject to the double taxation agreement. Employees not subject to source tax get no result.

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder; it collects no data.

open_questions.question: Is the specific nationality (and the spouse's nationality and country of residence) needed by any party, or only whether the person is Swiss / lives in Switzerland?

options: Ask only 'Swiss citizen yes/no' and 'lives in Switzerland yes/no'
open_questions.recommendation: Ask only the yes/no facts unless HR confirms it needs the full nationality.
